input.rationale: Section 13.5 correctly vests Developments (including software interface coding created solely by Corio) in Corio and includes a Commerce One assignment in the continuation at p0116, which matches our preferred position. However, the "unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One" carve-out flips ownership of IP that we create and fund over to the Vendor — a walk-away item (assignment of Customer IP to Vendor) that turns a support arrangement into a title transfer. Commerce One's pre-existing materials and its ownership of the Software (Section 2.8) are unaffected by the deletion, so the redline is minimal: strike the carve-out and repair the sentence that runs into p0116. The residual last sentence of p0116 (ownership of enhancements to the Software itself to be negotiated) is acceptable as an existing bargain, since those are derivative works of Commerce One's licensed Software. No Customer Data concept exists in this hosting/reseller agreement, so no data-ownership sentence is required.

proposal.summary: Delete the carve-out that transfers ownership of Corio-created Developments to Commerce One where Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We deleted the carve-out that would hand Commerce One ownership of Developments created solely by Corio whenever Commerce One supports them, since our position is that we own what we create and fund, with Commerce One retaining its pre-existing materials (as Section 13.5 already provides). If ongoing support is the concern, we can instead grant Commerce One a licence to use those Developments for support purposes.
